introduction: OverviewArabella IntroductionArabella is a 5✦ character from the Striker class and Instinct attribute.Deals DoT damage via the “Fracture” debuff, notably shining in AOE scenarios with respawning enemies and one central target to focus damage on.

Deconstruction Analysis: Increase Damage Amount of Arabella’s Fracture by 5% (max 6 stacks).

Liberated Memory

When Arabella activates Fractures that she inflicted, additionally inflict 1 Fracture on the target inflicted with Fracture Amplification.

Increase the max stack limit of Deconstruction Analysis by 4, and +50% Critical Damage to the Fractures that Arabella inflicts on the Fracture Amplification target.

panels.html:
Arabella Review

Pros

  • Great AoE damage.

  • Great DoT damage

  • Good Self-Draw options

Cons

  • Unable to deal Weakness Attack on her Fracture damage which is where a large portion of her damage comes from.

  • Can be very AP-expensive to play

  • Lacks ways to buff Fracture significantly

  • Single-Target damage not as good as her AoE damage.

Review

Introduction

Arabella is a 5-Star Instinct Striker Combatant who dominates the battlefield, torturing their enemies with Malice. Arabella is also the 3rd limited combatant, meaning they cannot be acquired via the standard banner once their banner ends.

Arabella’s playstyle is based around inflicting the “Fracture” debuff. “Fracture” is a debuff that activates during the end of the turn dealing damage for each “Fracture” the enemy is affected by. Arabella brings the ability to bypass the standard activation window for “Fracture” and ‘detonate’ them to deal upfront burst damage.  Arabella can easily inflict “Fracture” to all enemies, further enhancing her already solid AoE damage. 

Arabella has multiple different sources of damage in their kit that have varying different damage values, because of this - when deciding on what supporting units to pair with Arabella will depend on the deck that you’re planning on playing. “Fracture” deals one instance of damage whenever it triggers, as “Fracture”s damage value ramps quite quickly, seeking out combatants or buffs that offer multiplicative damage buffs will be valuable if you’re planning on triggering “Fracture” as many times per turn as possible. Additive Damage buffs can still be very beneficial to Arabella too, as many of her attacks are multi-targetting and also multi-hit, Arabella can still leverage these buffs extremely well. 

Review

Key Mechanics

Arabella’s goal is to inflict “Fracture” as much as possible on their enemies and triggering it via their “Hollow Verdict” or “Sadistic Restraint” cards to deal its damage upfront, instead of waiting until the end of the turn for it to activate. 

  • Fracture - Fracture is a stacking debuff that stacks up to a maximum of 30 times. Fracture activates at the end of the turn - dealing 40% DoT Damage for each stack of Fracture on that enemy, when activated it will decrease “Fracture” stacks by half..

  • Fracture Amplification - Fracture Amplification is a debuff that is applied to enemy units, whenever “Fracture” is inflicted to any enemy unit - the unit that is currently affected by “Fracture Amplification” is also given a stack of “Fracture”. If there is only 1 enemy, applies 2 “Fracture” instead and increases Arabella’s “Fracture” damage amount by 20%. “Fracture Amplification” can only affect 1 enemy unit at a time.

Synergies

Arabella Synergies

Cassius
Testing tag

Testing description

  • Cassius can generically buff a high amount while also having options that can give AP (via divines or neutrals).
  • Cassius’ draw can greatly help set-up and push for more aggressive damage optimizations for Arabella.
  • Cassius’ buffs are one of the best way to push Arabella’s many multi-hit Attack Card’s damage, as they have low ratios.
Narja
  • Narja is able to reduce the cost of Arabella cards, making them less expensive to play.
  • Narja can act as a pseudo-draw unit with Start of Turn Draw 2 epiphany on Shackles, but this is a very high-end and black-mass expensive set-up from its low Divine odds.
Hilde
  • Hilde can offer a high amount of draw, but it’s worth noting this often increases AP cost and lowers her value in other areas as a trade-off.
  • Hilde can apply a decent amount of Fracture. It’s worth noting that maximizing Fracture often comes at the cost of completely sacrificing Draw capabilities for Arabella.
Adelheid
  • Via divines can give AP, on-top of survivability and draw.
  • With E4, Adelheid can provide one of the largest buffs for DoT damage, Fracture included, and it’s completely passive and permanent for the battle. Making Adelheid one of the premiere supports for Arabella, unfortunately locked behind an Ego Manifestation, though.
Veronica
  • While worse than alternative options at giving AP, Veronica can offer much higher draw and still offer up to 4AP via Divine epiphanies a turn.
  • Veronica can buff via morale from Rosaria, a 4-star Partner.
Orlea
  • Using Sacred Censer, Orlea can provide a relatively high amount of multiplicative buffs for Arabella that increase her damage comparably to other buffers (but can peak higher with crits on big Fracture hits)
  • While Sacred Censer Orlea is rather good potential for damage, it's also quite inconsistent and AP expensive often forcing Arabella to use cost-reduction divines.

Seasonal

Arabella Seasonal Powers

Introduces Desire Cards. Desire Cards are cards that primarily exist to give a strong passive buff from meeting certain Desire Thresholds (3/5/7) which can only be done by having multiple ally decks also made in Season-4. 

  • For Desire Threshold, it’s common to run 1 Claim / 1 Survival / 1 Inquiry for use in a variety of builds; however, it's also common to just do 3 ‘X’ to meet effect easier or do 2 'X' / 1 Inquiry (to keep Sample Collection as Card Effect). This is extremely dependent on ally desire cards and individual team building goal.

!’X’ refers to a ‘Placeholder for Specific Desire Threshold Goal’, i.e. if you are building your team for 7 Claim then you might do 2 Claim / 1 Inquiry.

Introduces Persona Cards and Engravings. Persona Cards are powerful cards that introduce new playstyles or ways of buffing/debuffing. Engravings are effects that can be applied to both the Persona Cards and Equipment, functioning near identically to Refinements of Season-2 but with new effects.

  • There is no recommended Card Engraving, often times it will be specific to the team or skipped entirely (focusing just on Equipment Engravings). 

  • The most common Equipment Engraving to optimize for is [When 15 or more cards are in Graveyard, +15% Critical Damage to Attack Cards of this unit], but this effect does not stack, so other equipment Engravings that increase damage can also be used.

Introduces Refinements, effects on Equipment that allow one to get additional Equipment effects for no Faint-Cost (post-S2), and God’s Hammer, a powerful effect that gives a random copy of any other Equipment effect on-top of current Equipment but costs 10 Faint Memory and is only gained from the Boss.

  • There are no recommended specific Refinements.

+15% Critical Hit on Vulnerable, only works on Attack Cards, which makes it not synergistic with Arabella's main damage of Fracture.

Because God’s Hammer is completely RNG at the end of the run, we do not have a specific recommendation since the player has very little control over the decision but for ATK-based Attackers usually ATK% gear is considered best and DEF-based Attackers DEF% gear is considered best.

Introduces Forbidden Cards, powerful cards that create new synergies and can only be acquired once per run (can be duped at one event or via save data editing). 

  • Forbidden: Gesture of Freedom. Permanent Cost-Reduction to 1-card, can be manipulated.

  • Forbidden: Portrait of Fury. ++Draw, +Damage

  • Forbidden: Ecstasy of Violence. +Damage

100.00%
Arabella’s first Ego Manifestation “Sleeping Memory” improves their Mythic Card “The Art of Unmaking”. Improving the base damage dealt by an additional +50% and increasing the damage per debuff to 20% from 15% whilst also increasing the bonus damage cap to 180%. Provides a slight damage boost to their Mythic Card but ultimately doesn’t do much for their overall gameplan. Because this card is commonly removed, as is done in the deck used for calculations, it is not factored into the 'percentages' but if kept can be a small increase from its original.
Ego 2
106.29%
Arabella’s “Awakening Memory” grants Arabella an additional passive effect. Applies 1 “Fracture Amplification” at the start of battle to the enemy with the highest amount of AP. Additionally, whenever Arabella triggers her own “Fracture” through one of her own abilities, Arabella applies 3 stacks of “Fracture” to all enemies, up to 4 times per turn. This is a solid Ego for Arabella when being brought into Chaos/Sortie. Without refined Save Data this will help with ensuring Arabella is able to maintain “Fracture” on their enemies.
Ego 3
108.31%
Arabella’s “Vivid Memory” improves upon their Ego-Skill “Pathetic End”. Grants an additional +200% to the base damage, and increases the additional amount of fixed damage dealt by +20% - for a total of +50% additional fixed damage. The maximum cap per turn is also increased to 1500% of Arabella’s attack per turn, instead of 1000%. Very mediocre and overall doesn’t change their playstyle all that much.
Ego 4
116.23%
Arabella’s “Inner Memory” provides Arabella another passive effect. Whenever Arabella applies or triggers her own instance of “Fracture” via her own ability, Arabella gains 1 stack of “Deconstruction Analysis”. “Dismantle Analysis” can stack up to 6 times and increases Arabella’s “Fracture” DoT damage by 5% per stack. This is a solid source of increased damage for Arabella’s DoT damage, as finding buffs that directly increase DoT damage can be hard to find, but overall not worth investing for.
Ego 5
116.47%
Arabella’s Complete Memory Ego Manifestation is your standard Potential increase. Provides some slight extra damage output. Very standard.
Ego 6
143.74%
Arabella’s “Liberated Memory” grants Arabella another passive ability. Firstly, it increases the maximum stack count of “Deconstruction Analysis by 4. Whenever Arabella triggers her own “Fracture” through her own ability, Arabella applies 1 additional stack of “Fracture” to the target(s) who have been inflicted with “Fracture Amplification”. Additionally - Arabella's “Fracture” has an additional +50% Critical Damage against enemies who are affected by “Fracture Amplification”. This is by far Arabella’s best Ego, further increasing her “Fracture” generation on targets who have been affected by “Fracture Amplification” and providing a substantial amount of Critical Strike Damage to her “Fracture” debuff.

Scream For Me I: For gaining the most amount of Fracture as quickly as possible, this is one of the best epiphanies.

Scream For Me II: This being a multiplicative buff for Attack Card's is quite strange since many of Arabella's Attack Card base ratios are quite low, and a lot of her damage comes from Fracture, not Attacks.

Scream For Me III: The AOE Fracture Application on this can be quite high, making it a premiere option for maximizing Fracture on all Targets, rather than one main target.

Scream For Me IV: This is an amazing option for most builds as it increases Arabella's self-draw to reduce the deck-strain she has.

Scream For Me V: If you have a reason to apply a lot of different effects quickly, this can be nice, but there are usually avenues to do so through allies for Arabella herself that don't sacrifice her Fracture application card.

Neutral: Target Neutral: Morale 2. After turn-1, Arabella's recommended builds generally can hit max Fracture without needing Scream for Me I. This makes a neutral option that provides an additional buff, like Morale 2 very competitive.

Observer’s Pleasure I: While this can be used in AOE, the sheer amount of Fracture efficiency gained from the alternative AOE epiphany, Observer’s Pleasure IV, far surpasses this one’s additive bonus (~= 5 Morale) in many cases.

Observer’s Pleasure II: This being additive buffs makes it scaling with Fracture somewhat strange, but it is still a very solid epiphany that can push damage higher assuming you can compensate for Fracture application in some way.

Observer’s Pleasure III: The AOE Fracture and Vulnerable is quite nice, but the buff is a bit strange as it is a multiplicative buff to the base ratio of Attack Cards, but most of Arabella’s damage in her best builds will not be from Attack Cards. Moreover, Arabella’s best Attack Cards are low ratio attacks, which makes the additive buff strange.

Observer’s Pleasure IV: For AOE scenarios, this can be the best option as it allows for extreme efficiency on Fracture and high amounts to be applied in total. However, it will be rather lackluster in scenarios without AOE, which is almost all content currently.

Observer’s Pleasure V: This is the go-to epiphany as it is able to passively reset your Fracture Amplication at the start of every turn and apply the most amount of Fracture in non-AOE scenarios.

Neutral: Target Neutral: Vulnerable, Morale. Applying 1 Vulnerable or gaining 1 Morale is rather low value, especially considering alternative options can give the equivalent of 4-5 additional morale over the neutral morale epiphany AND ignore morale cap.

Sadistic Restraint I: Ability to trigger ally Fracture could be strong. The issue is there are no allies that can currently capitalize on this well, as even Hilde cannot make enough Fracture enough a turn to make this an especially viable build path.

Sadistic Restraint II: The go-to epiphany for Single-Target as it's a strong card by itself (being a 4-hit) on-top of being one of the best ways for activating a lot of Fracture quickly. This can also be a rather strong card for a multi-hit focused Attack Card build, alongside buffers like Cassius. It can enable the highest hit-count of any Arabella build.

Sadistic Restraint III: Defeat: is a very difficult condition to trigger, so this is a hard epiphany to make use of.

Sadistic Restraint IV: This is a kind of complicated card with a lot of set-up that has trouble getting adequate pay-off in current content. It could become stronger if we get a way to easily increase its cost and then decrease it, but at base it requires more effort to get less pay-off (in same number of hits) as Sadistic Restraint II

Sadistic Restraint V: This is recommended to be used alongside Sadistic Restraint II, as it is also important for maximizing hitcount in her Attack Card build.
